items.question_text: You have one project called proj-sa where you manage all your service accounts. You want to be able to use a service account from this project to take snapshots of VMs running in another project called proj-vm. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
To allow a service account from one project (proj-sa) to perform actions in another project (proj-vm), you must grant that service account the necessary IAM permissions directly on the target project.
Granting the 'Compute Storage Admin' role in proj-vm provides the specific privileges required to create, modify, and delete snapshots for VMs running within that project.
Options A and B are insecure and unnecessary workarounds, while Option D refers to legacy scopes that do not enable cross-project access.

choices.text: Download the private key from the service account, and add it to each VMs custom metadata.
Download the private key from the service account, and add the private key to each VM's SSH keys.
Grant the service account the IAM Role of Compute Storage Admin in the project called proj-vm.
When creating the VMs, set the service account's API scope for Compute Engine to read/write.

items.question_text: You created a Google Cloud Platform project with an App Engine application inside the project. You initially configured the application to be served from the us- central region. Now you want the application to be served from the asia-northeast1 region. What should you do?
items.solution_text: Google Cloud Platform enforces a one-to-one relationship between a project and an App Engine application, meaning each project can only host a single App Engine app. Additionally, the region location for an App Engine application is immutable once it is created; it cannot be changed after initial setup. Therefore, to serve the application from asia-northeast1, you must create a new GCP project and initialize a new App Engine application within that project with the desired region.

choices.text: Change the default region property setting in the existing GCP project to asia-northeast1.
Change the region property setting in the existing App Engine application from us-central to asia-northeast1.
Create a second App Engine application in the existing GCP project and specify asia-northeast1 as the region to serve your application.
Create a new GCP project and create an App Engine application inside this new project. Specify asia-northeast1 as the region to serve your application.

items.question_text: You need to grant access for three users so that they can view and edit table data on a Cloud Spanner instance. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
The `roles/spanner.databaseUser` role is required to view and edit table data, whereas `roles/spanner.viewer` only provides read-only access.
According to GCP IAM best practices, you should assign roles to groups rather than individual users to simplify permission management and reduce administrative overhead.

choices.text: Run gcloud iam roles describe roles/spanner.databaseUser. Add the users to the role.
Run gcloud iam roles describe roles/spanner.databaseUser. Add the users to a new group. Add the group to the role.
Run gcloud iam roles describe roles/spanner.viewer - -project my-project. Add the users to the role.
Run gcloud iam roles describe roles/spanner.viewer - -project my-project. Add the users to a new group. Add the group to the role.

items.question_text: You create a new Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster and want to make sure that it always runs a supported and stable version of Kubernetes. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
To ensure a GKE cluster *always* runs a supported and stable version, you must enable automatic updates, as manual selection only sets the initial state. Node Auto-Upgrades automatically manages the Kubernetes version lifecycle by upgrading nodes to the latest available stable version when it becomes ready.

Node Auto-Repair (A) fixes broken nodes but does not upgrade software versions. Selecting the latest version at creation (C) is a one-time action that does not guarantee future compliance. Container-Optimized OS (D) affects the node's underlying OS, not the Kubernetes control plane or kubelet version management.

choices.text: Enable the Node Auto-Repair feature for your GKE cluster.
Enable the Node Auto-Upgrades feature for your GKE cluster.
Select the latest available cluster version for your GKE cluster.
Select "Container-Optimized OS (cos)" as a node image for your GKE cluster.

items.question_text: You have an instance group that you want to load balance. You want the load balancer to terminate the client SSL session. The instance group is used to serve a public web application over HTTPS. You want to follow Google-recommended practices. What should you do?
items.solution_text:
Option A is the correct choice because HTTP(S) Load Balancing is Google's recommended solution for public-facing web applications and provides built-in SSL termination capabilities.

In contrast, SSL Proxy and TCP Proxy load balancers are designed for non-HTTP traffic or scenarios requiring end-to-end encryption where the proxy does not decrypt the payload, while Internal Load Balancers are restricted to private network communication.

choices.text: Configure an HTTP(S) load balancer.
Configure an internal TCP load balancer.
Configure an external SSL proxy load balancer.
Configure an external TCP proxy load balancer.
